lead.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin plan their first three-way meeting next week in Shenzhen, with nuclear arms cuts on the table
lead.short: Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin plan to meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen late next week, the White House said. Trump "will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world", spokeswoman Olivia Wales said. Iran may also come up, but not Ukraine. Moscow and Beijing have not commented.

why.text: It would be the first meeting of the leaders of the three biggest nuclear powers since their last arms treaty lapsed.

more: Trump arrives in Shenzhen late on Wednesday for the two-day summit of 21 member states, and holds bilateral talks with Xi on Thursday, their fourth meeting since he returned to office in 2025. His trip also includes a summit of South-East Asian nations in the Philippines on Tuesday. No agreement is expected from the three-way meeting, a senior US official told the AP and Reuters.

The last nuclear arms treaty between the US and Russia expired in February, leaving the world's two biggest arsenals without major limits. Trump has said he could replace it with a better deal that includes China, which has been building up its arsenal. Former senior US officials told the BBC that bringing in Beijing and Moscow could take years.

facts.agenda: nuclear arms reduction; Iran possibly; not Ukraine

seconds.headline: Microsoft restores Outlook, Teams and Copilot after a day-long outage in over 70 countries, blaming a network upgrade
seconds.short: Microsoft said on Saturday that its services had been fully restored after a worldwide outage that hit Outlook, Teams and Copilot in more than 70 countries. The company apologised and said the fault was introduced during a "network capacity upgrade" and was not a cyber-attack or an AI agent. More than 430 million people use the affected products.

why.text: One faulty upgrade stopped work at governments, courts and hospitals, a reminder of how much runs on a few cloud providers.

more: Users began reporting problems with Microsoft 365 on Thursday. By Friday the outage had reached the Japanese government, the Philippines Supreme Court, Australia's spy agency, and trains, hospitals and courts in North America. Staff at the US House of Representatives said it set back a day of legislative work, and in India it disrupted work for many on Friday.

In Britain, parts of the NHS, some schools and police forces were affected, though cyber minister Liz Lloyd said the impact on frontline services such as 999 calls was "limited". Canada's national rail network warned passengers they might not get email updates. Services began to recover on Friday afternoon, UK time, nearly 24 hours after the problems began.

facts.cause: a network capacity upgrade, per Microsoft

update.new: Services are restored, and Microsoft names the cause.
update.front: The outage that stopped work worldwide is over, and Microsoft says a bad upgrade caused it.

seconds.headline: A minibus carrying college students collides with a truck near Kaziranga, killing 26 people
seconds.short: Twenty-six people died when a minibus and a container truck collided head-on at Rangajan on National Highway 715 near Kaziranga National Park on Friday, Assam minister Ranoj Pegu said. Many of the dead were college students returning from classes. Officials suspect the minibus, travelling from Golaghat to Nagaon, was speeding.

why.text: It is one of the year's deadliest road crashes, on a highway through a national park that carries heavy traffic.

more: Twenty people were taken to hospitals in Jorhat and Golaghat, and two of them died. Seven of the 18 still being treated are in intensive care at Jorhat Medical College Hospital in a critical condition, and 11 are stable, Pegu said. The state government will pay for their treatment, and doctors from Guwahati and Dibrugarh have joined the teams.

Post-mortems are being carried out on Saturday at the civil hospital in Golaghat, after which ambulances will take the bodies home. Chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma is to meet the families and the injured in Golaghat district on Saturday. An investigation into the cause is under way.

seconds.headline: A telecommunications failure grounds every departing flight in the US for hours, the longest such stop in 25 years
seconds.short: The US Federal Aviation Administration halted all departing flights nationwide on Friday afternoon after a telecommunications outage hit the centres that guide cross-country air traffic. Airspace reopened at 8.15pm Eastern time after more than four hours, the longest ground stop in 25 years and only the second nationwide halt of all departures since 11 September 2001.

why.text: It exposed how fragile America's air traffic system is, with weekend sports teams and holiday travellers among those stranded.

more: "Everybody's safe," Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said, adding that there were no suspected cyber-attacks. "It's going to be slow," Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy warned, as flights depended on available pilots and crews. More than 4,700 flights were cancelled and 10,000 delayed on Friday, and 700 had already been cancelled for Saturday, according to FlightRadar24.

At least 827 flights were diverted, 670 of them back to where they started, according to the aviation analytics firm Cirium. Planes already in the air were allowed to land, and international flights were handled case by case. The Trump administration blamed "overloaded" systems. About 11,000 flights carrying 1.5 million passengers had been due to leave after 4pm Eastern time, Cirium said.

stories.headline: India wants Bangladesh's army to fly Sheikh Hasina home, and sets conditions for her return, BBC Bangla reports
stories.short: India is looking to send Sheikh Hasina back to Bangladesh and wants the Bangladesh army to take responsibility for bringing her home, preferably on a military aircraft, BBC Bangla reported. The former prime minister has been sentenced to death by a Bangladeshi court over the crackdown on protesters in July 2024, and India has set Dhaka two conditions.

why.text: Sheltering a leader condemned at home has strained India's ties with Dhaka, and her return could be dangerous for her.

more: The first condition mirrors her arrival: she fled to India on 5 August 2024 aboard a Bangladesh military aircraft. India's preferred option had been for Hasina to move to a third country, but repeated efforts failed, the report said. India has faced criticism for sheltering a leader convicted over the deadly crackdown.

Hasina has said she plans to return in December, without naming a date, and has asked for a new passport. "Look, I understand the risks very well. I may be arrested the moment I arrive. They may send me to prison. They may even try to kill me," she told Reuters.

facts.first condition: Bangladesh army to bring her back, ideally by military aircraft

update.new: India sets conditions for sending her back.

stories.headline: The Nvidia scandal turns on Howard Lutnick, as Treasury says Commerce sat on sanctions against Alice Huang's company
stories.byline: THE TIMES OF INDIA · BBC · 14 NOV
stories.short: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Thursday that Treasury, State, the trade office and the war department had wanted Megaspeed, the company linked to Alice Huang, on the US entity list for months, "but commerce has the pen". The comments put Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who oversees chip exports, under pressure.

why.text: The question is no longer one man's affair but whether Washington let advanced chips leak to China.

more: "I am frustrated when President Trump made it very clear that China should not receive any Nvidia chips above H100s," Bessent said. "Any leakage is very frustrating." Lutnick had argued that America should sell enough chips to China to get it "addicted to the American technology stack". A Chinese company founded by Alice Huang obtained banned Nvidia chips, Bloomberg reported.

Huang misled Nvidia's top lawyer about the affair, Reuters reported, citing sources. Nvidia has approached Arm's chief executive, Rene Haas, about succeeding him, Reuters also reported. Huang had met Trump repeatedly and flew with him on Air Force One to China in May, the BBC noted.

update.new: The scandal moves to Lutnick and chip exports.

stories.headline: SpaceX aborts its first attempt to catch both halves of Starship, and the booster burns up in the Gulf
stories.short: SpaceX abandoned its attempt to catch Starship's Super Heavy booster with the launch tower's mechanical arms on Friday, diverting it to the ocean, where it came down in flames. The 124m rocket had lifted off from Starbase in Texas at 16:45 local time. The upper stage went on to orbit, and SpaceX may try to catch it on Saturday.

why.text: Catching both stages is how SpaceX plans to make Starship fully reusable and cut the cost of reaching space.

more: "Safety is always the number one priority, and we're still testing out things that we haven't done before," a SpaceX spokesperson said. The upper stage, the Ship, is deploying 26 Starlink satellites and is due to complete 14 orbits before returning to the tower 22.5 hours after launch, at about 15:15 local time on Saturday.

SpaceX has caught the booster on three earlier test flights, but the upper stage, which reached orbit for the first time only in September, has never been caught. SpaceX said it would decide on the catch after checking the vehicle in space, and can bring it down in the ocean instead.

facts.ship catch: possible at about 15:15 local time Saturday

stories.headline: Goalkeeper Jesús Owono is banned for 12 matches over the collision that killed Tenerife's Jesús de Miguel
stories.short: The Spanish football federation has banned FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono for 12 matches, the maximum sanction, over the collision in which Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel was fatally injured on 2 November. De Miguel died the next day. The disciplinary committee cited the raised leg and the "forcefulness of the impact", which the referee called excessive.

why.text: It is the heaviest penalty Spain's rules allow, and the goalkeeper, 25, has not decided whether he will play again.

more: "It is public knowledge that the tragic outcome of the events was the death of Jesus de Miguel Alameda," the committee said, adding that the seriousness of the case justified "the imposition of the sanction at its maximum level" under Article 102 of the disciplinary code. Fines also apply.

Owono, an Equatorial Guinea international, has withdrawn from his national squad. "We will give him space so that he feels completely free to make any decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return," said Andorra manager Carles Manso, adding that Owono was spending time with family and friends.
